clause: For each expansion route: the LITERAL query or URL that produced it — the text that was typed, not a description of the search
quote: Five moves, each with its literal query or URL and result recorded
reason: The literal-query-not-a-description proof standard is current law in R-0250; expansion routes conceived under the stuck protocol carry it. Not carried nowhere.

clause: A hunt report with an EMPTY expansion section FAILS THE ITEM (same consequence as 'nothing further')
quote: Every hunt report carries an EXPANSION section listing routes that did not exist at session start
reason: The expansion section is a required output ('carries an EXPANSION section ... its own numbered item and never last'); an empty required output is a failed one, and R-0253 names docs/report-contract.md as the binding close-out contract that enforces it.

clause: A newly conceived route that returns NOTHING is a REPORTED SUCCESS — the invention is the deliverable, not the yield
quote: listing routes that did not exist at session start — how each was conceived, what it returned, where else it applies, and whether it was recorded
reason: A zero-yield newly-conceived route is still a listed route with its return recorded; the reporting obligation is carried and 'is a success' is rationale for why it is listed rather than dropped.

clause: Side quests remain forbidden and become tracker rows; writing the row is the whole response
quote: everything else is recorded on the frontier with evidence and left
reason: Out-of-scope discoveries are recorded and left rather than chased (R-0273); R-0253 also holds expansion 'is never a side quest.' The don't-chase / write-it-down / move-on mechanism is carried.

clause: A session citing RULING 88 while building infrastructure has committed a scope breach and reports it as one
reason: Anti-pretext application of the scope-discipline rule carried by R-0273 ('The denominator is finite and stated at the start ... Discretion covers how, never what: ... an unrecorded amendment to the brief'). The specific instance (citing the expansion mandate to justify infrastructure) is rationale, not a distinct standalone bar.

clause: A source walked but not recorded is a DEFECT (next session re-derives it)
quote: A walk is counted or it did not happen.
reason: An unrecorded walk is treated as not having happened (forcing re-derivation), and R-0252 makes re-derivation the exact harm ('none re-derives it, so a wrong sentence in the store costs every session after it').

clause: Next-session report answers: why did that procedure not run, and what changed so it runs next time
quote: A founder find is a class-wide defect in the discovery process, handled like any named instance: what would have found it, and where else that applies.
reason: The root-cause ('what would have found it') plus durable class-wide prevention ('where else that applies') carry the three-question structure; the exact question wording is rationale form.

clause: Absorbing the find as a new manifest entry and moving on is NOT an adequate response
quote: An item closed at the instance and open at the class is not done.
reason: The anti-pattern (fixing only the named instance) is exactly barred; R-0253 also frames a founder find as 'a class-wide defect ... handled like any named instance.'

clause: A session in the wrong environment says so IMMEDIATELY and does the subset it can
quote: A brief says which kind it is — local-required (credentials, live network, production) or remote-capable — and the session confirms before item one.
reason: Immediate detection is carried by 'confirms before item one'; the 'do the subset you can' fallback is carried by R-0273 skip-forward ('one blocked item never qualifies while other work exists').

clause: A DISALLOW is not a WALL — re-walking a disallow on a clock is asking again after being told no (do not re-check a disallow on the freshness clock)
quote: Permission and transport are orthogonal.
reason: A disallow is a PERMISSION fact; a wall is a TRANSPORT fact, kept orthogonal in R-0250. The 14-day re-walk expiry in R-0250 attaches only to 'walled sources,' not to disallows, so a disallow is not on the freshness clock.

clause: Each row carries the TIER it sits at under RULING 84
quote: Every route carries a tier, and the tiers are walked in order, always.
reason: The tier is a universal route attribute in R-0249; a sources.md source is walked as a route, so the tier travels with it even though the successor register column list emphasizes status/access/licence/adapter/last-walked.

clause: Each source is also a route in docs/branch-manifest.md: sources.md answers 'what exists / may we use', the manifest answers 'what do we walk and in what order' — both, every time
quote: Before any state's hunt begins, its free sources are enumerated into the manifest as state-scoped routes.
reason: Both instruments persist as current law — R-0263 makes docs/sources.md the permission/existence register, and R-0249 mandatorily enumerates every source into the manifest as a walked route with an order. The two-file division of labour is carried.

clause: Continue alternate compliant retrieval methods for the permission document, AND alternate compliant branches to the underlying public fact — a blocked route may never become a blocked fact
quote: A route can fail; the record obligation cannot. `ROUTE_BLOCKED → NO_SOURCE_FOUND → COMPLETE` is forbidden for a record known or expected to exist.
reason: A blocked route never becoming a blocked fact is core acquisition doctrine; the dual-track (keep hunting the permission document AND the underlying fact) is carried by R-0250 'CANNOT_TELL fails safe for the route and keeps hunting the fact by other branches.'

clause: What is still owed is the REPLACEMENT (RULING 206 replacement obligation on each held artifact), which is an engineering obligation, never a Needs Sean / author decision, and never a precondition for using the held text
quote: One representation lost is a replacement obligation, never a loss and never a blessing.
reason: The replacement obligation is carried by R-0248; 'never a precondition for using the held text' is carried by R-0253 'Captured public-record text is kept and used'; that it is engineering work (a route portfolio) and not an owner decision follows from R-0248 treating acquisition as the machine-executable hunt and R-0271 holding NEEDS SEAN as a parallel lane that never satisfies the obligation.

clause: Permission is established per DOCUMENT HOST, never per portal (a document URL's host is frequently not the portal host)
quote: the shared fetcher, which refuses any host recorded `no` or `unknown`
reason: Permission is keyed and enforced per host by the shared fetcher (R-0263/R-0253), and R-0248 holds 'A failure on one host is a fact about that host' — the vendor/portal is not the record and permission attaches to the document host.

clause: Do NOT add advocacy organizations, PACs, or endorsement sites as sources — go to the underlying government filing
restoreText: Advocacy organizations, PACs, and endorsement sites are never added as sources; the underlying government filing is the source of record for a candidate's positions and finances.
reason: A distinct source-selection/neutrality prohibition. R-0255 forbids INFERRING positions from endorsements (a rendering rule) and R-0249 orders official sources first but excludes nothing; neither prohibits INGESTING a partisan org as a source. Carried nowhere.

clause: Where terms require attribution (LegiScan CC BY 4.0), the attribution ships WITH the data it describes
restoreText: Where a source's licence requires attribution (e.g. LegiScan CC BY 4.0), the attribution ships with the data it describes wherever that data renders.
reason: R-0263 records 'licence obligations' as a register column but no active ruling carries the operative licence-compliance rule that required attribution renders adjacent to the data. This is a legal compliance bar, not operational detail, and is carried nowhere as an action obligation.

clause: A dead endpoint is recorded as dead rather than deleted (e.g. Google Civic Representatives)
quote: `docs/sources.md` is the live register: one row per source with status (wired / evaluated / not in use)
reason: The register is persistent and status-bearing, so a dead endpoint becomes a status row rather than a deletion; the never-delete norm is reinforced by R-0250 'stale is never deleted' and R-0252 'A rejected candidate is retained as rejected.'

clause: A body that is serving is NOT NOT_ATTEMPTED; where the registry contradicts what is published the registry is STALE and the drift is a finding
quote: Stale is re-walked before it is relied on; stale is never deleted. A record that cannot say when it was measured reads as stale.
reason: The practical harm — a registry entry contradicting live publication being relied on — is caught by R-0250's stale-is-re-walked rule, and R-0264 requires every production-serving tenant to resolve to a registered body, so a serving-but-unattempted phantom cannot stand. Registry-vs-reality drift surfaces as the finding these together compel.

clause: A rotated key is proven DEAD and the new one proven LIVE, by CALLING both (a host may answer a dead key with HTTP 200)
quote: A credential is proven by calling it, never assumed.
reason: The proof-by-calling standard is current law; the 'a 200 can lie' insight is carried by R-0250's control-query rule ('A 200 that is not about the thing asked for is not a document'). Proving both keys is the application of proof-by-calling to a rotation.

clause: A scrub is cleanup, never the fix; a value written to a synced folder must be assumed read; rotation is the fix
restoreText: A leaked credential is remediated by rotation, never by scrubbing alone; any value written to a synced folder is assumed already read, and the compromised value is rotated dead.
reason: R-0265 carries secret PREVENTION (never reaches transcript/log/commit; guard is the actual values) and rotated-credential persistence, but no active ruling carries the REMEDIATION doctrine that a leaked value must be rotated and a scrub is insufficient. A distinct security bar carried nowhere.

clause: Credential creation/rotation/scope changes are reported by NAME, PROVIDER, CONTEXT, SCOPE, ACTOR, OWNER-COPY LOCATION; a report missing any of those six fields FAILS the session report gate
restoreText: Every credential creation, rotation, or scope change is reported by name, provider, context, scope, actor, and owner-copy location, and a report missing any of the six fails the session report gate.
reason: R-0265 covers secret handling and rotated-credential persistence, and R-0271 names escalation-request fields for a different event (an ask). Neither carries the transparency/audit reporting obligation and gate for a credential change actually performed under autonomous operation. Carried nowhere.

clause: Enumerated failure classes: acquisition, extraction, identity, linkage, retrieval, evidence selection, synthesis, validation, rendering, accessibility, interaction, freshness.
reason: The failure-class concept is carried by R-0268 ('a red question generates a typed diagnostic WorkItem carrying its failure class'). The specific 12-label enumeration is an operative taxonomy that lives in the typed WorkItem, not in constitutional text.

clause: Red never defaults to "go acquire"; the failure class is diagnosed first.
quote: a red question generates a typed diagnostic WorkItem carrying its failure class
reason: Requiring a red to produce a typed diagnostic carrying its failure class is diagnose-first by construction and precludes defaulting straight to acquisition.

clause: Negative controls carry their authority, period, and verified-through scope.
reason: The known-answer control set is carried by R-0268 ('TRUTH ... permanent, continuous, unannounced, measuring false absence and false presence') and R-0274 (the auditor is scored by the control set). Per-control metadata (authority, period, verified-through scope) is operational construction detail of the control set; control staleness is governed generally by R-0250.

clause: The window promotes only items of record classes the activation gate has opened (per-record-class granularity).
reason: The activation-gate discipline is carried by R-0268 ('Until the activation gate opens the window runs in SHADOW and promotes nothing ... only the latter [INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCED] counts toward activation'), and every promotion is verified on the served surface with regression reverting the batch. The substance (nothing unproven reaches readers) is preserved; per-record-class opening granularity is a control-plane implementation property of how the gate opens.

clause: The unit of conservation is the LOGICAL RECORD, never the document (one .ics file is one raw row and many events; count in the unit the disposition happens in).
quote: Extraction conserves: `produced + dropped + outOfWindow + duplicates === logicalInput`, exactly.
reason: The conservation equation's unit is 'logicalInput' — the logical record, not the raw document — which encodes the definition. The .ics example is rationale.

clause: A contest with one side approached and the other not is a BREACH, named as one, with the unapproached side listed - never a percentage.
quote: reconciled per contest so anyone can see at a glance that both sides were approached
reason: Per-contest reconciliation surfaces each contest's approached/unapproached sides at a glance — exactly the name-the-unapproached-side, never-a-percentage mechanism. A one-sided contest is visible per contest rather than hidden in an aggregate rate.

clause: Nothing collected before the line is ever SHOWN to anyone as signal - not a sample, aggregate, chart in a buyer deck, or screenshot in a pitch.
quote: Nothing collected before that line — organic-looking or not — is ever sold or shown to anyone as signal.
reason: R-0259 carries 'sold OR shown to anyone as signal' verbatim in substance — the successor did not narrow to 'sold.' The prohibition on display-as-signal (deck/pitch/sample) is preserved.
